newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower awaiting export sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower awaiting export sales.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower as the market floundered while awaiting direction from the export sector, traders said.
The market was stirred early this week by talk India and Egypt were entering the market for optional-origin wheat. But the market was skeptical the U.S. will land much, if any of the business.
"We have a lot of competition," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
There was talk India could be seeking at least 50,000 tonnes and as much as 750,000 tonnes. Also there was talk Egypt this weekend may be in for 400,000 to 800,000 tonnes.

European exporters said France could sell between 200,000 and 300,000 tonnes to Egypt and Alex Nichol, spokesman for the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said Wednesday Australia is pursuing further sales of wheat to India and Egypt.
Dry weather in the U.S. Great Plains was mentioned but there were some forecasts for rain there early next week.
Cargill Inc sold one million bushels of July and Lee B. Stern and Co. sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat closed 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1/2 higher, with March down 2-3/4 at $3.70-1/4.
Chart watchers cited a bearish slant for the March, May and July contracts stemming from the four- and 20-day moving averages.
The first resistance level early Wednesday for the March was at $3.74-1/2 a bushel and second resistance was at $3.77-3/4. The session high was at $3.75-1/2.
First support for the March was at $3.71-1/4 and second support was at $3.68. The session low for March was $3.70.
Wheat futures volume, according to the CBOT, was estimated at 10,000 contracts, about the same as the 10,449 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 500 March $3.60 puts at three cents, bought 200 March $3.80 calls at 4-1/2 to 4-5/8 cents and bought 100 March $3.90 calls at 2-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, below the 5,466 traded Tuesday.
